Create a typed table

Source: R/zutable.R
zutable.Rd

zutable() builds a table from named vectors, recycling only those of length one. Each column's type is inferred from its vector (see schema()); na() declares a column to be filled later with a typed missing value. as_zutable() converts a data frame or a list, inferring the types or checking the columns against schema. Row names are not kept.

Usage

zutable(...)

as_zutable(x, schema = NULL)

is_zutable(x)

Arguments

...

Named column vectors.

x

A data frame, a list of columns, or a zutable.

schema

A schema from schema() to check x against, or NULL to infer one.

Value

A zutable. is_zutable() returns TRUE or FALSE.

Details

Values enter exactly or not at all: strings are converted to UTF-8, a POSIXct with no time zone is given "UTC" (it already counts from 1970 in UTC), and a value a type cannot hold, such as a date with a fraction of a day or NA in a not_null() field, is a zutable_value_error.

Examples

zutable(id = 1:3, name = c("Ada", "Linus", "Grace"), score = NA_real_)
#> <zutable> 3 rows x 3 columns
#>   id      name     score
#>   <int32> <string> <float64>
#> 1 1       Ada      NA
#> 2 2       Linus    NA
#> 3 3       Grace    NA
as_zutable(data.frame(x = 1:2), schema(x = not_null(int32)))
#> <zutable> 2 rows x 1 column
#>   x
#>   <not_null(int32)>
#> 1 1
#> 2 2
